title: Non-interventional, retrospective/prospective, multicenter registry to document the treatment practice of patients with STIC (serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma) or STIL (serous tubal intraepithelial lesion) in clinical routine
summary: Serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma (STIC) and serous tubal intraepithelial lesion (STIL) refer to tissue changes in a woman’s fallopian tubes that are classified as precursors, particularly of ovarian cancer and other malignant pelvic tumors. Clear treatment and follow-up guidelines for patients with STIC/STIL are lacking. The STIC registry collects information about STICs and STILs to address this data gap. Based on the collected data, future diagnostic and therapeutic steps will be defined to improve the care of patients. Due to the rarity of these tissue changes, every hospital and medical clinic in Germany is called upon to enroll patients with STIC and STIL in the registry.
conditions: Carcinoma in situ: Other and unspecified female genital organs

Inclusion criteria:
Confirmed diagnosis of STIC/STIL regardless of stage, treatment form, and line of therapy.
Exclusion criteria:
- Missing histological confirmation
- Missing informed consent (prospectively enrolled patients)
